issues.legal_issue: A right to guardianship under personal law is not enforceable through a constitutional petition unless it is a fundamental right guaranteed by Part III.
material_facts: The petitioner claimed a right under personal law to act as guardian of his minor children.
A competent court had appointed another person as guardian of the minors.
The petitioner sought relief under Article 32, including custody of the minors according to personal law.
issues.conclusion: The claimed personal-law right to guardianship was not a fundamental right, so Article 32 could not be used to enforce it.
issues.legal_principle: Article 32 empowers the Court to grant relief only to enforce rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution. The Court relied on Article 32 and Part III; it cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.constitutional_enforcement_petition: A person brings a constitutional petition seeking enforcement of an alleged right.
predicates.claimed_right_is_personal_law_guardiansh: The petitioner claims a right to guardianship arising under personal law.
predicates.claimed_right_is_part_three_fundamental_: The claimed right is guaranteed as a fundamental right by Part III of the Constitution.
predicates.personal_law_guardianship_right_not_enfo: A personal-law guardianship right that is not a Part III fundamental right cannot be enforced through the constitutional petition.

issues.definition: When a constitutional petition seeks to enforce a personal-law guardianship right that is not a Part III fundamental right, the right is not enforceable through that petition.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of denial of equality or equal protection cannot be based on the decision of a competent judicial tribunal.
material_facts: A competent court appointed a guardian for the minors and rejected the petitioner's application for appointment.
The petitioner alleged that the appointment deprived the minors of equal protection of the laws.
issues.conclusion: The judicial appointment did not amount to discrimination or a denial of equality or equal protection that could be challenged on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: A claim of denial of equality before the law or equal protection may be made against executive action or legislative process, but not against a decision of a competent judicial tribunal. The Court relied on the constitutional equality guarantee and cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.constitutional_equality_claim: A person alleges that action denied equality before the law or equal protection of the laws.
predicates.challenged_action_is_competent_tribunal_: The action challenged is a decision made by a competent judicial tribunal.
predicates.equality_claim_not_available_against_jud: A constitutional equality claim cannot be maintained against a decision of a competent judicial tribunal.

issues.definition: If a constitutional equality claim challenges a competent tribunal's decision, the equality claim is unavailable against that decision.

issues.legal_issue: A constitutional petition cannot enforce a right that a competent court has already negatived by adjudication.
material_facts: A competent court appointed another person as guardian and rejected the petitioner's application.
The petitioner appealed, but the appeal was dismissed, and the order became final.
The petitioner later sought under Article 32 to enforce the guardianship right that had been rejected in those proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Article 32 petition could not be entertained to enforce a right already negatived by the adjudication of a competent court.
issues.legal_principle: Relief under Article 32 for enforcement of a right requires proof of the right and its infringement. Where adjudication by a competent court has negatived the claimed right, Article 32 cannot be used to enforce it notwithstanding that adjudication. The Court relied on Article 32 and cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.constitutional_enforcement_petition: A person brings a constitutional petition seeking enforcement of an alleged right.
predicates.claimed_right_was_adjudicated_by_compete: A competent court previously adjudicated the claimed right.
predicates.adjudication_negatived_claimed_right: The previous adjudication rejected the claimed right.
predicates.constitutional_petition_cannot_enforce_n: A constitutional petition cannot enforce a right that a competent court has already rejected.

issues.definition: When a constitutional petition seeks a right already adjudicated and rejected by a competent court, the petition cannot enforce that right.

issues.legal_issue: A constitutional petition cannot be used to circumvent the rejection of an application for special leave to appeal.
material_facts: The petitioner sought special leave to appeal against the order dismissing his appeal, and the application was rejected.
The petitioner then sought relief under Article 32 concerning the same guardianship dispute.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the special-leave application could not be circumvented by filing a petition under Article 32.
issues.legal_principle: An order rejecting an application for special leave under Article 136 cannot be circumvented by an application for a writ under Article 32. The Court relied on Articles 136 and 32 and cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.constitutional_enforcement_petition: A person brings a constitutional petition seeking relief in a dispute.
predicates.special_leave_application_was_rejected: An application for special leave to appeal concerning the dispute was rejected.
predicates.petition_seeks_to_reopen_same_dispute: The constitutional petition seeks to reopen the dispute addressed by the special-leave application.
predicates.constitutional_petition_cannot_circumven: A constitutional petition cannot be used to circumvent the rejection of an application for special leave to appeal.

issues.definition: If a constitutional petition seeks to reopen a dispute after special leave to appeal was rejected, it cannot be used to circumvent that rejection.

issues.legal_issue: Claims to assess and recover loss to property, determine liability for misappropriation or negligence, or ascertain property interests are not suitable for determination in a constitutional petition seeking enforcement of fundamental rights.
material_facts: The petitioner alleged that a guardian had misappropriated or misapplied the minors' property and that the State had failed to protect it.
The petitioner sought assessment of the loss and compensation from the respondents.
The petitioner also sought ascertainment of the minors' property and its custody.
issues.conclusion: The claims for assessment of liability and loss, compensation, and ascertainment of property had to be pursued through a properly constituted civil suit or proceedings under the Guardian and Wards Act, not through an Article 32 petition.
issues.legal_principle: Article 32 provides relief for enforcement of fundamental rights; claims to assess liability for loss to an estate may be pursued in a properly constituted suit, while property entitlement may be ascertained in proceedings under the Guardian and Wards Act or in a civil suit. The Court relied on Article 32 and the Guardian and Wards Act; it cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.constitutional_enforcement_petition: A person brings a constitutional petition seeking relief.
predicates.claim_requires_assessing_property_loss_o: The claim requires determining property entitlement, assessing loss, or deciding liability for alleged misappropriation or negligence.
predicates.property_loss_and_liability_claim_requir: A claim requiring assessment of property loss or liability must be pursued through an appropriate ordinary civil proceeding rather than the constitutional petition.

issues.definition: When a constitutional petition presents a claim requiring assessment of property loss or liability, that claim must be pursued through an appropriate ordinary civil proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A change in circumstances requiring alteration of a guardianship order must be raised before the court that made the order rather than through a constitutional writ petition.
material_facts: A District Court had made an order appointing a guardian of the minors.
The petitioner asserted that events occurring after that order necessitated its modification.
The petitioner sought relief from the Supreme Court under Article 32.
issues.conclusion: If later events required modification of the guardianship order, the petitioner had to apply to the District Court for relief rather than seek a writ under Article 32.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a party seeking modification of a guardianship order because of later events should apply to the court that made the order. It relied on Article 32 and the proceedings under the Guardian and Wards Act; it cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.constitutional_enforcement_petition: A person brings a constitutional petition seeking relief concerning a guardianship dispute.
predicates.guardianship_order_was_made_by_lower_cou: A lower court previously made an order appointing a guardian.
predicates.later_events_are_said_to_require_modific: The petitioner asserts that events after the order require it to be changed.
predicates.modification_request_belongs_before_orde: A request to modify the order because of later events must be made to the court that issued it.

issues.definition: If later events are said to require changing a lower court's guardianship order, the modification request belongs before the court that made the order.

issues.legal_issue: A person cannot represent minors as their next friend in proceedings when another guardian has been appointed unless the court permits that person to act.
material_facts: A District Court had appointed a guardian for the minor petitioners.
The first petitioner claimed to act as their next friend in the constitutional petition.
He had not obtained an order permitting him to act as next friend despite the existing guardianship appointment.
issues.conclusion: The first petitioner could not claim to act as the minors' next friend without the required permission of the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Order 32, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs who may act as next friend and permits the court, for reasons recorded, to allow another person to act when a guardian has been appointed. The Court relied on Order 32, Rule 4; it cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.proceeding_on_behalf_of_minors: A person brings a proceeding on behalf of minor children.
predicates.another_guardian_has_been_appointed: A court has appointed someone else as guardian of the minors.
predicates.proposed_next_friend_lacks_court_permiss: The person seeking to act as next friend has not obtained the court's permission to do so.
predicates.proposed_next_friend_cannot_act_for_mino: A person without the required court permission cannot act as next friend for the minors in those circumstances.

issues.definition: When another guardian has been appointed and the proposed next friend lacks court permission, the proposed next friend cannot act for the minors.
